newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BERLIN STADIUM TO GET FACELIFT FOR WORLD CUP BID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BERLIN STADIUM TO GET FACELIFT FOR WORLD CUP BID.

text.p: The mayor of Berlin pledged on Monday to modernise the city's Olympic Stadium as part of Germany's bid to host soccer's 2006 World Cup.
"Berlin will have a stadium worthy of the World Cup by 2006 in the form of the Olympic Stadium," Mayor Eberhard Diepgen wrote in a letter to the German Soccer Federation (DFB).
European soccer's governing body, UEFA, will decide by the end of 1998 whether to back Germany's or England's bid for the tournament.

The Berlin stadium, built for the 1936 Olympics, has fallen into disrepair although it still hosts athletics meetings and the German soccer cup final. It is also home to the city's second division side Hertha Berlin.
